And this custom has remained among them until this day.
And it is right to know
that King John the Keraite was not rejected without cause,
but after he turned his heart away from the love (fear) of Christ his Lord Who had magnified him,
and took a wife from a certain nation among the nations of the Chinese which is called Qara-Khitai.
And when he abandoned the fear of his fathers and served foreign gods,
therefore God took the kingdom from him and gave it to one who was better than he,
and whose heart was upright with (before) God.
And at that time a certain man from among the Tatars appeared,
who in the middle of winter,
in all that frost and cold which exists in that land,
would go naked and wander about in the mountains and heights for many days.
And he would come and say:
"I went to God,
and He said to me:
'Behold, I have given the whole earth to Temüjin {OCR?} and to his sons,
and I have called his name Genghis Khan.'"
Because his former name was Temüjin.
And this man the Tatars called Teb Tenggeri.
Concerning the sons of Genghis
Khan:
Genghis Khan had many sons and daughters,
but the great and renowned ones were those who were born of the great queen.
And to this his great queen,
whose name was Börte Fujin {OCR?},
she had four sons.
The first:
Jochi.
The second:
Chagatai.
The third:
Ögedei; the fourth:
Tolui.
And Jochi he made the head of the hunt,
because hunting is loved and honored among them more than any other work.
And Chagatai the head of the law,
which they call the Yassa,
he appointed.
And to Ögedei he committed the administration of the kingdom.
And Tolui the youngest he placed as director of the armies and the warriors.
And to each one
he showed a specific land for their dwelling.
